sources.citation: Marck, Jeff. 2000. Topics in Polynesian language and culture history. Pacific Linguistics 504. Canberra: ANU. doi:10.15144/PL-504
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Family-level only (p. 74): 'Polynesian languages usually have penultimate stress which was certainly a feature of Proto Polynesian.. The main formal exception was word-final long vowels or double morae where the long vowel or double morae as a whole was stressed.' Rurutu (RUT) and Tubuai (Tub) occur only as language abbreviations / kin-term sources; no Austral-specific stress statement.

sources.citation: Hancock-Teed, J. Drew & Mary Walworth. 2021. Reo Ra'ivavae (Ra'ivavae, Austral Archipelago, French-occupied Polynesia) - Language Snapshot. Language Documentation and Description 20: 154-161. doi:10.25894/ldd48
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing; no phonology. Sec. 4: 'There is little existing descriptive literature on Reo Ra'ivavae' - names Stimson's unpublished 1930s dictionary ms., Schooling 1981 wordlist, Zamponi 1996.

sources.citation: Charpentier, Jean-Michel & Alexandre François. 2015. Atlas linguistique de la Polynésie française / Linguistic Atlas of French Polynesia. Berlin: De Gruyter Mouton & Papeete: Université de la Polynésie française. 2562 pp. (open access, doi:10.1515/9783110260359)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online (also online with a university library login)
sources.note: Phonology/transcription chapter (pp. 39-43) gives consonant inventories and correspondences for Rurutu (#17, 8 consonants) and Ra'ivavae (#18, 8 consonants incl. [g]); the only stress remark (p. 43, 'l'accent tonique frappe l'avant-dernière syllabe') is about Hiva Oa Marquesan reduplications. 'Les Australes' section (pp. 64-66 FR / 116-117 EN) is sociolinguistic. Nothing on Austral word stress.

sources.note: Describes Rapa (a different language); mentions Rurutu only for its 7-consonant inventory (author's 2010 Rurutu data) and Ra'ivavae geographically; nothing on Austral stress.
